title: Angles and lines
lede: Angles are measured turns. A handful of rules about straight lines and parallel lines solve most angle puzzles.

sections.md:
## Measuring a turn
An **angle** is formed by two rays from a shared point (the **vertex**). It's measured in **degrees**: a full turn is 360°.

| Name | Size |
|---|---|
| Acute | less than 90° |
| Right | exactly 90° (the little square in the corner) |
| Obtuse | between 90° and 180° |
| Straight | exactly 180° |
| Reflex | between 180° and 360° |

## Angle pairs
- **Complementary** angles add to **90°**.
- **Supplementary** angles add to **180°**. Angles side by side on a straight line are supplementary.
- **Vertical angles** are the opposite angles where two lines cross. They are always **equal**.
- Angles all the way around a point add to **360°**.

## Parallel lines and a transversal
When a line (the **transversal**) cuts across two parallel lines, it makes 8 angles but only **two different sizes**. Every angle is equal to one size or the other, and the two sizes add to 180°.

- **Corresponding** angles (same position at each crossing) are equal.
- **Alternate interior** angles (inside the parallels, opposite sides of the transversal, a Z shape) are equal.
- **Co-interior** angles (inside, same side, a C shape) add to 180°.

## Triangles
The three angles of any triangle add to **180°**. Tear the corners off a paper triangle and line them up: they make a straight line.

For any polygon with n sides, the interior angles add to **(n − 2) × 180°**. A square: 2 × 180 = 360°. A hexagon: 4 × 180 = 720°.

sections.title: Find the missing angle
sections.problem: A triangle has angles 47° and 68°. What is the third?
steps: Angles in a triangle add to 180°.

sections.title: Use a straight line
sections.problem: Two lines cross. One angle is 112°. Find the other three.
steps: The angle next to it is supplementary: 180 − 112 = 68°.
Vertical angles are equal, so the opposite angles are 112° and 68°.

sections.label: Puzzle habit
sections.md: In an angle problem, label every angle you can find in one step, even if the question didn't ask for it. The answer is usually two or three easy steps chained together.

practice.q: Two lines cross. Vertical angles are…
options: Equal only if the lines are parallel
practice.why: Opposite angles at a crossing match.

practice.q: A triangle has angles 90° and 38°. Find the third.
What do the interior angles of a pentagon (5 sides) add to?
Parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle is 70°. Which sizes appear among the 8 angles?
practice.why: Only two sizes, and they add to 180°.
